deltas.basis: **Delta:** each tool has one typed declaration: name, description, argument type/schema, result type/schema, visibility and scope classification, mutation and audit requirements, blocking bound, and a typed handler binding. The registry derives listing, lookup, timeout metadata and invocation from that declaration. Missing or duplicate declarations and unclassified tools fail construction. C2 supplies typed handlers through interfaces; C1 never imports C2's package. There is no reflection-based dispatcher or raw-JSON forwarding between handlers.

**Delta:** replace `decodeOne`/`strictUnmarshal`, the separate admin object walker and C2's permissive decoder. Decode before deriving scope-sensitive behavior, audit targets or defaults. A validated admin call contains validated typed arguments and its public audit target; C2 then checks live authority and records intent/outcome.

**Delta:** declare `run_check` as a scoped read with args `{repo,ref?,files?}`. `repo` is canonical; absent `ref` selects the default branch head. `files` is an optional array of `{path,content}` UTF-8 overlays confined to regular authoring files: 1–32 files, 1 MiB total, no symlinks or parent traversal. C11 reads `--local` into these bounded overlays. Result is `{ok,repo,ref,object_sha,commit_sha,selected_file,spec_digest,plan, findings,checks}`; unavailable SHA/digest/plan facts are null, never invented. `findings` entries are `{path,code,reason,remedy,command?}`; `checks` entries are `{name,state}` with `state=offline|snapshot_checked|live_required|unknown`. `ok` means all required checks passed; unknown/live-required is not a pass. C2 authorizes and calls C3 inspect mode; no acceptance, run, Workflow, token, declaration write or audit mutation occurs. C4 is the sole validator.

deltas.basis: **Delta:** bind route-only access operations to the same typed grant operation, with no parallel dispatcher. Storage, credential handling and bootstrap remain with their owning components.

Public DTOs have explicit snake_case tags after authorization/redaction. Collections are objects such as `{"runs":[]}`, `{"repositories":[]}` and `{"grants":[]}`. Empty collections are arrays. Dictionary keys are untouched. `promote` acknowledges `{id}` with optional requested follow-up state; issue deletion acknowledges `{id,deleted:true}`. **Delta:** remove post-serialization reflection and renaming; tag the run detail and its projections directly. The published snake_case shape already exists and remains the sole spelling.

**Delta:** display the immutable admitted step plan supplied by C2/C4. `step_count` describes the complete logical inventory, independently of paging; `steps_planned_exact` distinguishes an exact total from a lower bound. Every planned leaf is present immediately. Unreached entries display pending, without adding a run status. Retries fold into their plan entry while retaining native attempt/node/container identities for logs. Literal loops expand in the plan; dynamic loops and recursion expand their placeholder in place and show `≥N` until exact. Structural nodes are not steps. The affected tools are `run_get`, `run_list`, `status`, `wait` and `run_wait`; the UI run list and run detail use the same projection. One step has one UI log part with its attempts. C1 does not compute a second plan. Public run fields are `object_sha` (accepted object) and `commit_sha` (tested checkout), without a `sha` output alias. `publish_retry` descriptions refer to passed logical steps and complete bound attempt evidence, with no grouping vocabulary.

deltas.basis: The `events_wait` arguments carry `repos`, `refs_glob`, `kinds`, `own`. C2 applies actor scope first. `EventPage` carries `events`, `next_after_id`, `latest_id`, `oldest_id`, `has_more`, optional `gap`; waits add timeout information. Events carry `id`, `kind`, `at`, public run/promotion/repository/ref/SHA identity, summary and bounded data; internal deduplication keys stay hidden. **Delta:** use the eight kinds in [Shared contracts](README.md#shared-contracts), including observation-only `run.updated`, owned by the component recording each fact. The filter is `events_wait.kinds`. C2's [Events and observation](c2-service-actions-and-history.md#events-and-observation) defines its payload `{run_id,repo,ref,object_sha,commit_sha,data?}`, internal count pair in `Data`, revision dedupe key, fact-and-event transaction without coalescing, and separate 24-hour/newest-10,000 progress retention. C1 preserves those semantics and cursor gaps; it emits no independent update events. Delivery is at least once. Clients deduplicate IDs and continue with `next_after_id`, including on empty filtered pages and timeout. Push and `run://<id>` resource notifications are observations. Reconnects resume with `Last-Event-ID`; gaps/backlog limits are explicit, never completion evidence. `GET /mcp` must not silently reset a supplied old/future Last-Event-ID cursor to the current head; use C2's cursor contract.

deltas.basis: **Delta:** `repo add` accepts normal SSH, SCP-style SSH and HTTPS forge addresses with the forge's own SSH user, a path of any depth and an optional `.git` suffix. As in Git, a relative SCP-style path of a user other than `git` is in that user's home and is stored as `ssh://user@host/~/path`; an absolute SCP path and a `git@` SCP path keep the root form. A new upstream stores the address without its last part; that namespace's last directory is the organization. The user and every path part are letters, digits and `._-`, start alphanumeric and hold no `..`, and only a leading `~` names the home; passwords and tokens are refused, and an address without a user logs in as `git`. Existing upstream addresses retain their stored scheme, user, host, port and namespace and match only an address with the same user. Discovery is a live scoped read: a joined caller binds exactly one visible registered match without an admin call, names ambiguous candidates and prints a usable administrator command when the repository is unavailable. `--upstream` selects among visible matching addresses; it never turns the supplied address into only a path selector.

Its pack commands use the server SSH endpoint saved by join, pinned by the Oberth server's SSH host keys that the selected profile saved at install or join (`--known-hosts` replaces them); without them `repo add` refuses and names `--known-hosts`, and join asks for a new invitation, and `~/.ssh/known_hosts` is never read. An administrator binding clears only the product's stale uplink binding.

deltas.basis: **Delta:** After commit, wake waiters by closing/replacing a channel; register before read, then wait, so a concurrent commit cannot be missed. Event reads capture an upper cursor and scan `(after,upper]`, at most 500 internally and 200 publicly, filtering scope before output. Advance past examined filter misses; never skip unexamined matches. Pages carry events, next_after_id, latest_id, oldest_id, has_more and gap. A pruned cursor requires a snapshot. Progress retention is separately 24 hours or newest 10,000, whichever removes first. Ordinary events are kept for 30 days; C11 calls retention once a day. Streams and waits are observations only. Completion/timeout reads durable state again. sync_status shows current native holders/waiters/stale units only, without stored intervals.

rows.name: events_wait

Its source-result negative control expects reason "result of a source step is not readable" and remedy "write the value to a file and use an output parameter"; the file-output alternative runs with real source delivery. `ungranted-secret` prints the exact operator command, `grant` runs it unchanged, and a repeated `push` succeeds. `TestExactNativeCapabilitiesContract` refuses each native workload kind and Oberth namespace even with a matching grant. `TestExactGrantedSourceAndSecretPathsContract` checks image pull Secrets; `TestGrantedMountPathsContract` exercises every allowed volume and an unlisted type, authored tokens and protected executor patches. Ordinary artifacts, labels and downwardAPI volume cases remain positive controls. `TestPreparedPlanCoversActualControllerLeaves` permanently compares the prepared plan with the real Argo controller. The grant tests refuse store-path/Kubernetes-Secret substitution and unlisted projected sources, and admit granted pull secrets with shared templates. `TestPreparationPlanContract` covers roots, hooks, loops, retries, referenced templates, case-sensitive fields and collapsed dynamic placeholders. Each boundary test starts from admissible YAML and changes one forbidden feature.
rows.reason: Refuse an execution-requesting push before acceptance with every knowable YAML offender and exact grant action; structural validation distinguishes live-required authority.

deltas.basis: **Delta:** Every received push ends accepted or rejected; a transport exit leaves no third outcome. Accepted means admitted, prepared and committed: its exact objects and attribution are retained and delivered once, immediately after acceptance, even if its reply is lost or the pusher's connection is gone. Delivery does not wait for a reconnect or restart. Rejected means public refs are restored, the reservation is rejected durably and nothing is delivered. A late client or transport failure cannot reverse an accepted push.

**Delta:** the method signatures, value types and three typed Git errors are pinned in [Shared contracts](README.md#shared-contracts). `internal/gitport.Git` is the only cross-component Git port; C11 injects a C6 adapter, and C2 wraps it in its own consumer interface. No concrete cache import is required by C2, C3 or C10. Pure identity validation lives in `internal/reponame`.

deltas.basis: - Authorization has two in-flight calls per verified Workflow and a global `SourceClientBurst/3` bound; excess returns immediately. Caller authentication and recorded Workflow ownership are checked; the sealed admission decides what source the run may load. There is no repeated admission, replay computation or authorization-result cache at Load. A busy export refusal does no Git or repository locking. None of these limits gates run submission. More than 16 flooding Workflows can delay another tenant's Loads; no isolation guarantee is claimed. **Delta:** retain one Git/compression slot, release it before network writes, and bound active staged transfers separately at two. Archives are request-private, with no persistent cache or cross-request reuse.

deltas.basis: - Main delivery contains regular files plus sanitized detached `.git` history, index and the recorded checkout snapshot. Never export hooks, remotes, credentials, private refs or repository configuration. Main skips symlinks/gitlinks; pins reject them and contain no `.git`. Pins are private copies at admitted `/work/sources/<name>` under the same source guarantees; at most four, each 128 MiB / 4096 files. Main is 512 MiB including delivered metadata. Pack output and traversal metadata each retain their 512 MiB guards; no source ref-count or undeltified-history cliff. Exact file reads are at most 1 MiB and paths at most 4096 bytes. **Delta:** pack overflow is a terminal 403, not an endless 503 retry.

deltas.basis: - Active snapshots outlive concurrent ref release and GC; repository locks never span network sink writes. Cancel, close and join owned workers. Export has one 10-minute total deadline and one-minute write bounds; authorization phases have 10-second bounds. Reconcile uses bounded owner pages inside the existing GC pass. **Delta:** staged archives cap main at 544 MiB and pins at 160 MiB (payload limit plus 32 MiB framing allowance). Two main archives plus a 512 MiB pack and 256 MiB metadata reserve require 1856 MiB below the chart's 2 GiB default scratch limit. Stream blobs directly into local archives; remove Git scratch before releasing its slot. Directories/files are 0700/0600. Startup removes owned interrupted exports before serving; cleanup failure refuses startup. C9 guards configured chart capacity.

Store applies C2's ordinary event retention separately from progress retention. Events retain monotonic IDs, dedupe keys and ascending exclusive `after_id` reads. The eight-kind envelope is pinned in [Shared contracts](README.md#shared-contracts); scope IDs and dedupe keys stay internal. **Delta:** implement C2's [Events and observation](c2-service-actions-and-history.md#events-and-observation), including a projection revision and its event written with the fact, plus separate progress retention. Preserve cursor order and replay across restarts; notices never authorize work. The fact writer supplies the events; C2 owns reconnect/reset semantics. Use the existing endpoint-seek bounds query, not a full event scan.

**Delta:** C2's neutral-file import preserves issue numbers, open/closed state, text, original authors, timestamps and ordered history in the ordinary issue records, with an imported mark and provenance. It creates no synthetic run, CI selector or CI reconciliation obligation. Native issues and imported manual issues share the same later read, edit and close paths.

**Delta:** The grants baseline is schema 5, with only current records, constraints and query indexes and no configured release-role records. A layout pin for each schema number preserves its baseline digest; changing the layout requires a new number. Do not transplant the migration catalog. Future migrations keep immutable IDs, transactional receipts and unknown-ID refusal, including when numeric counts match. Daemon/admin open requires the exact supported schema; explicit creation and maintenance remain distinct. Opening a missing admin database must never create one.

deltas.basis: **Delta:** Encrypted backups use age with the operator's age backup key. A backup preserves an encrypted database copy for safekeeping. Its archive is authenticated and complete: decryption and C7's inspection recover the snapshot and its matching report; dry runs write nothing. The destination directory is trusted to its writers; there is no protection against a concurrent directory writer. Before publication or failure cleanup, the staging path must still name the written file, as an accident check. Cleanup authority ends at its first successful unlink. Publication is a hard link that never overwrites; a filesystem without hard links refuses with the remedy "write to a local disk, then copy". A dry run refuses a missing destination directory. Backups contain the database, not installation keys. The bundled store's contents are in no backup, and install gives the operator no administrator token for it. After a store loss, put the secrets again. Review and `oberth backup` state this gap and show `oberth access list --json` as administrator to list granted secret paths; keep that name list beside the database backup. It contains no secret values. There is no store snapshot command or store-administrator recovery procedure in this version, and no shipped offline inspection command.

deltas.basis: **Delta:** An installation marks only namespaces it creates and never updates an existing namespace. Namespace role and holder checks read the native releases, including their installed namespace, stored manifest and recorded answers; marks alone are not proof. A namespace rendered by any chart's release is held, regardless of chart identity. Refuse a namespace held in either role by another release. An existing installation keeps its recorded pipeline namespace. During apply, before the first cluster write, save namespace and port answers so an interrupted install can resume. Explicit answers may replace that record only when no release revision exists; a pending or deployed revision must agree with its recorded answers.

deltas.basis: 7. **Delta:** **Defaults and review.** Baseline Pod defaults and the link-local egress filter are on by default and shown in review; the operator may turn either off. The Pod defaults set native main and executor containers to drop all capabilities, disable privilege escalation and use RuntimeDefault seccomp. A pipeline namespace created by this installation uses Pod Security `baseline`.
